suspicions.claim: The _limit helper returns max_limit when limit equals max_limit instead of the requested limit value, changing behavior for exact-limit requests.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/posts?limit=25 and read pagination.limit in response; expect 25 but may get 25 (no change) — however if max_limit differs from default, the bug appears. To see the bug, use an endpoint with a different max_limit (e.g., a custom paginated route with max_limit=10) and request limit=10; pagination.limit will be 10 before PR but 10 after PR (still same). suspicions.claim: If pagination dict lacks 'limit' key, pagination.get('limit', max_limit) returns max_limit, then _limit returns max_limit — identical to old behavior where limit defaulted to max_limit then was capped to max_limit.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/posts (no limit param) and read pagination.limit; should be 25 (default max_limit). No change.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s2_no_limit sent GET /api/posts without limit param and both base and head returned 200 with identical pagination data

suspicions.claim: The helper does not validate that limit is an integer; a non-integer limit could cause TypeError in comparison limit > max_limit, whereas old code would also fail but at a different line.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/posts?limit=abc and observe error status; both versions likely return 400 validation error from schema before reaching decorator.
